  │ i looked at this on mobile and its a no go. not at all.                   
                                                                              
  Right on both counts. GIMP made every panel a floating window; everyone else
  made one window with                                                        
  navigation inside it. This platform hands authors GIMP, so that is what gets
  built — and a window                                                        
  manager on a phone is unusable, full stop.                                  
                                                                              
  Two kernel changes have landed to make this buildable. Read them first; they
  are the whole                                                               
  premise of this issue.                                                      
                                                                              
  ## What the kernel now provides                                             
                                                                              
  1. A view no longer declares pixels (mesh-web  f08dd7b ).  ViewDecl  carried
  tile ,                                                                      
   defaultSize ,  minSize  and  closable  at the top level — four of its six  
  fields describing window                                                    
  furniture. They moved into an optional  window  object that a windowed      
  chrome reads and a routing                                                  
  chrome ignores entirely, losing nothing.                                    
                                                                              
  2.  cx.display  (mesh-web  ec3a54c ). How much room there is, as a signal:  
                                                                              
    readonly needs = needs('display');                                        
    const { width } = cx.display.size();   // re-runs on resize               
                                                                              
  Deliberately a size and not  isMobile . A width is a fact; what to do at    
  380px is a decision, and it                                                 
  is this chrome's decision. Do not add a device check.                       
                                                                              
  ## Build a  nav  chrome in mesh-core                                        
                                                                              
  An Extension providing  PAGE_CHROME , alongside the existing  chrome  rather
  than replacing it.                                                          
  Same  ViewDecl s, same applications, different shell.                       
                                                                              
  • Narrow: one view at a time, filling the surface. Navigation between views 
  — a rail, a tab bar,                                                        
  whatever reads well. No frames, no dragging, no resize grips, no mode switch.
  • Wide: your call, and say why in the plan comment. Falling back to the     
  window chrome is                                                            
  legitimate; so is keeping one view and adding a sidebar. What is not        
  legitimate is a breakpoint                                                  
  nobody can find.                                                            
  • The transition matters. Dragging a browser narrow must not lose which view
  is showing.                                                                 
                                                                              
  ## Routing is the part with no prior art here                               
                                                                              
  There is no router in mesh-web — no  hashchange , no  pushState , nothing.  
  windows.open({ view })                                                      
  is the only navigation and it is not addressable: no URL, no back button, no
  shareable link.                                                             
                                                                              
  Decide in your plan comment, before writing it, whether the router belongs  
  in this chrome or in the                                                    
  kernel. Arguments both ways, and I do not think the answer is obvious:      
                                                                              
  • In the chrome: it is a presentation concern, and a windowed chrome does   
  not want one.                                                               
  • In the kernel: every chrome will want it, and two chromes with two URL    
  schemes is worse than one.                                                  
                                                                              
  Whichever you choose, back must work and a URL must be shareable. That is   
  the test.                                                                   
                                                                              
  ## Not in scope                                                             
                                                                              
  • Changing the existing  chrome  extension                                  
  • Folding catalog/releases/sites/fleet into one app — real, and its own     
  issue                                                                       
  • Anything in mesh-web. If the kernel is missing something, say so in a     
  comment rather than reaching                                                
  for it.                                                                     
                                                                              
  ## Setup                                                                    
                                                                              
    npm update @flybyme/mesh-web                                              
                                                                              
   npm install  alone serves a cached git dep and reports "up to date". Check 
  the installed version is                                                    
  0.15.11 or later, or  cx.display  will not exist and none of this is        
  buildable.

    Desired and observed sit next to each other on every row and are never merged.
    There is deliberately no healthy column anywhere in this system, and this screen
    is why that works: health is the difference between what a machine should run
    and what it is running, and showing both says more than a flag could. A row that
    reads '2 running, 3 assigned' with 'not running: builder' underneath is the
    whole diagnosis.
    
    One node.status call covers the table -- it returns a summary for every node --
    rather than one observed lookup per machine, which would be seven round trips
    arriving at different times and flickering between disagreeing states.
    
    Stopping a service asks first, through the confirmation capability. That is the
    first consumer of the thing destructive was waiting for.
